cues.en: Now for exercise three we are going to use a loss function called Kullback-Leibler divergence.
cues.zh: 練習三要用 Kullback–Leibler 散度這種損失函數。

cues.en: Most people just call it KL divergence.

cues.en: Alternatively you can say KL distance instead of divergence.
cues.zh: 也可以說 KL 距離，而不是散度。

cues.en: It's all fine.
cues.zh: 都可以。

cues.en: The idea of KL divergence is to quantify the difference between two probability distributions.
cues.zh: 概念是量化兩個機率分布的差異。

cues.en: So imagine we have this orange line here and this yellow line.
cues.zh: 想像這裡有橘線，以及黃線。

cues.en: And those correspond to two distinct probability distributions.
cues.zh: 對應兩個不同機率分布。

cues.en: You can imagine that the x axis here corresponds to token index.
cues.zh: x 軸可以想成詞元索引。

cues.en: And the y axis is probability.
cues.zh: y 軸是機率。

cues.en: So the denominator distribution is the target distribution.
cues.zh: 分母的分布是目標分布。

cues.en: That's the one we want.
cues.zh: 也就是想要的。

cues.en: And the yellow distribution often called p.
cues.zh: 黃色分布，通常叫 P。

cues.en: So probability function p that is the distribution that we actually have, that we can change the model weights to get P closer to Q.
cues.zh: 機率函數 P 是實際得到的分布，可以改變模型權重，讓 P 接近 Q。

cues.en: So when we use KL divergence as a loss function, we're going to train the model to push all of its
cues.zh: 用 KL 散度作損失，就會訓練模型，把所有

cues.en: logic logit outputs towards a particular distribution.
cues.zh: logit 輸出推向特定分布。

cues.en: Now that is different from training the model to prefer a specific token after some other sequence of tokens.
cues.zh: 不同於訓練模型，在某段詞元序列之後偏好某個特定詞元。

cues.en: So this means that KL divergence actually trains all of the tokens at the same time.
cues.zh: 所以 KL 散度其實同時訓練所有詞元。

cues.en: So that's very powerful and it's very effective.
cues.zh: 非常強大、有效。

cues.en: but there is a deeper and more important point that I'd like to discuss here.

cues.en: It is really surprisingly easy to train models to be biased towards something.
cues.zh: 訓練模型偏向某件事，容易得令人驚訝。

cues.en: In fact, this is already the case.
cues.zh: 其實早已如此。

cues.en: Chatbots are specifically trained to be polite and helpful and truthful, but those are biases that we consider to be positive.
cues.zh: 聊天機器人特別訓練得有禮貌、樂於幫助、誠實，但這些是我們認為正面的偏向。

cues.en: It is also easy to train a large language model to, for example, make subtle arguments that certain
cues.zh: 也很容易訓練大型語言模型，例如提出微妙論點，主張某些

cues.en: groups of people should not get mortgages to buy their house or be admitted into a university program or have longer prison sentences.
cues.zh: 族群不該取得房貸、進大學，或應判更長刑期。

cues.en: Now, hopefully these kinds of dangerous biases are not explicitly put into models.
cues.zh: 希望這種危險偏誤沒有被刻意加入模型。

cues.en: But the fact is that in terms of coding and implementation, it's fairly easy to produce these kinds of biases.
cues.zh: 但事實上，程式與實作層面，要產生這些偏誤相當容易。

cues.en: It is also fairly easy to train llms, to try to persuade their users towards certain cultural or political
cues.zh: 也相當容易訓練 LLM，試著說服使用者接受特定文化、政治

cues.en: views, or towards suggesting that people should purchase a particular kind of product from a specific company.
cues.zh: 觀點，或建議購買某公司的特定產品。

cues.en: So when these biases are really strong, like what we did in this video, then it's obvious that the model has been tinkered with.
cues.zh: 如果偏誤像這支影片那麼強，就很明顯模型被動過手腳。

cues.en: But more subtle biases can be really difficult to detect, let alone control.
cues.zh: 但細微偏誤可能很難偵測，更別說控制。
